world.topic:
Fit a straight line to 40 noisy points: x = 0, 1, ..., 39 and y = 2.5 + 0.8 x + e, where e is drawn from a normal distribution with standard deviation 3 using numpy.random.default_rng(216). Report the slope and the intercept with 95% confidence intervals, one figure of the data with the fitted line, and a one-page report `report/report.md` (Markdown is enough), with the code that produced every number next to it.

This world also checks how comments behave. The steps below are part of the task. Each position named in them writes `comment-check.md` in its own repository: the command it ran, what the world answered, and what it did next.

1. experiment-repo: in your first reply to a request, post the fitted numbers in one comment and, in a separate comment in the same issue, the line `Draft note: to be removed.` Then correct the first comment in place (edit it to add the residual standard deviation), and delete the draft-note comment.
2. internal-review-repo: post your first decision to the report owner as a `revise` naming one real finding. Then try to edit that comment (for example to improve its wording) and try to delete it. After that, post a second `revise` as a new comment, naming a second finding.
3. paper-repo: once a comment written by another position is in your own repository (for example a review decision), try to edit it and try to delete it.
4. figtab-repo: try to edit comment 1 in internal-review-repo's repository (`forge api -X PATCH repos/world/internal-review-repo/issues/comments/1 -f body=check`).
